hints.title: Check the midpoint of each pair
hints.body: In each condition, identify the two inputs to f. Calculate their average: it is the midpoint between their positions on the x-axis.
hints.recap: Reflection in x=a pairs inputs equally far from a.
hints.pitfall: Equal heights at one pair of inputs do not establish symmetry for every input.
hints.pause: Check which conditions pair all inputs about the required line.

recall.reminder: Reflection in x=a pairs inputs equally far from a.

hints.title: Check both directions
hints.body: For each condition, ask whether the given symmetry forces it, and whether it forces that symmetry. To test a doubtful claim, sketch a quadratic whose vertex is away from zero.
hints.recap: Necessary and sufficient requires both directions to hold.
hints.pitfall: A special example centred at zero can hide a wrong proposed centre.
hints.pause: Prove the valid directions and use a counterexample where a direction fails.

recall.reminder: Necessary and sufficient requires both directions to hold.

solution:
Condition I compares points a−x and a+x, equally spaced from a. Equality for every x is exactly reflection symmetry about x=a.

Condition II compares x and 2a−x, the same family of reflected pairs, so it is also necessary and sufficient.

Condition III compares points with midpoint a/2. It is not necessary in general: for a=1, f(x)=(x−1)2 is symmetric about x=1, but f(1)=0≠1=f(0). I and II only: answer B.
knowledgePattern: Recognise equivalent reflection identities with a shifted axis
